candidates.original_title: A randomized field trial of the Pathway Project cognitive strategies approach to text-based analytical writing for mainstreamed English learners in secondary school
candidates.description: The Pathway Project cognitive strategies professional development program improves academic writing outcomes for secondary school Latinos and English learners
candidates.citation_sentence: This prior study yielded effect sizes of .35 in Year 1 and .67 in Year 2 on an on-demand assessment of academic writing. It also showed that the Pathway Project had a small but statistically significant impact on the writing subtest of the California Standards Test (CST; Kim et al., 2011; Olson et al., 2012).
candidates.notes: [ling26: no entry matched this anchor] Year 2 of the AUHSD replication; original SAUSD study identified as Kim et al. (2011) and Olson et al. (2012); no DOI available for the original study in the paper.

candidates.original_title: Enhancing the interpretive reading and analytical writing of mainstreamed English learners in secondary school: Results from a randomized field trial using a cognitive strategies approach
candidates.description: A cognitive strategies approach to text-based analytical writing improves the academic writing performance of mainstreamed Latino English learners and other secondary students.
candidates.citation_sentence: Results from earlier studies (Kim et al., 2011;Olson et al., 2012;[36][38] suggest that integrating strategy instruction within a text-based approach to analytical writing can enhance Latinos' and ELs' writing ability.
candidates.notes: The replication was conducted in a different urban, low-SES school district and included Years 1 and 2. The authors explicitly state that the study largely replicated the earlier randomized controlled trial; AWA effects were significant in both years, while CAHSEE effects were described as suggestive.
